import hashlib
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.db import connection, connections

CORE = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "rhinoCore"
MIGRATIONS = "".join(sorted(p.name for p in (CORE / "migrations").glob("[0-9]*.py")))
TEMPLATE_DB = "api_tpl_" + hashlib.sha1(MIGRATIONS.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]  # a new migration means a new template


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def django_db_setup(django_db_blocker, worker_id):
    # Migrate once into a template DB, then give each xdist worker its own copy: seconds instead of 228 migrations.
    db = settings.DATABASES["default"]
    worker_db = f"test_api_{worker_id}"  # worker_id is "master" when xdist is off
    with django_db_blocker.unblock(), connection._nodb_cursor() as cur:  # Django's own cursor on the "postgres" DB
        cur.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(7007)")  # one worker builds the template; released when cur closes
        cur.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = %s", [TEMPLATE_DB])
        if cur.fetchone() is None:
            cur.execute(f'CREATE DATABASE "{TEMPLATE_DB}"')
            db["NAME"] = TEMPLATE_DB
            call_command("migrate", verbosity=0)
            call_command("createcachetable")  # settings.CACHES uses the database_cache table
            call_command("loaddata", str(CORE / "fixtures" / "initial_data_prod_aws.json"), verbosity=0)
            connections.close_all()  # CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE needs no open sessions on the template
        cur.execute(f'DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "{worker_db}"')
        cur.execute(f'CREATE DATABASE "{worker_db}" TEMPLATE "{TEMPLATE_DB}"')
    db["NAME"] = worker_db
    yield

api-tests:
    name: API Tests
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    needs: check-changes
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    env:
      ENV: QA
      RHINO_IS_RUNNING_UNIT_TESTS: 1
      POSTGRES_HOST: localhost
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CLOUD_TEST_POSTGRES_PASSWORD }}
      # ...the rest of the `test` job's env block (a YAML anchor would keep the two jobs in sync)
    services:
      postgres:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/postgres:17.6
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
        env: { POSTGRES_DB: rhino_cloud, POSTGRES_USER: rhino, POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${{ secrets.CLOUD_TEST_POSTGRES_PASSWORD }}" }
        command: -c fsync=off -c synchronous_commit=off -c full_page_writes=off
        options: --health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Run the API layer
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        run: |
          uv sync --frozen --group api-tests --no-install-project
          .venv/bin/pytest tests_api -n 4 --junitxml=reports/junit.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with: { name: api-tests-reports, path: cloud/rhinoCloud/reports/ }

title: [BE] FakeTaskQueue for Celery with a contract suite on a real worker
what: A fixture that records every Celery task the code sends (by replacing app.send_task) and a drain() that runs them in-process, oldest first, plus a contract suite that runs the same scenarios on a real Celery worker with Redis.
why: Eleven test classes in rhinoCore/tests set CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER, which Celery's docs say is not suitable for testing: tasks run inside the caller and skip the broker's serialization (ours is pickle). Recording and then draining keeps both the order and the serialization honest.
how: Create tests_api/fakes/task_queue.py (sketch) and a `task_queue` fixture that does `monkeypatch.setattr(app, "send_task", queue.send_task)` on the app in rhinoCore/celery_tasks/app.py. Task.apply_async ends in app.send_task, so RhinoTask's header injection still runs.

Serialize arguments with kombu using app.conf.task_serializer and accept_content (pickle and json in rhinoDjango/settings.py), the way a broker would, so an argument that can't be serialized fails in the test.

drain() runs each task with Task.apply and the recorded headers (RhinoTask restores the metadata context from them), re-raises the task's own error, and follows Celery's `chain` option, which vocabulary_indexing.index_large_vocabulary and the NVFlare inference flow use.

Contract suite tests_api/contracts/test_task_queue_contract.py (marker `contract`): a plain task, a chain, an error, the metadata context kept. The real side uses celery.contrib.testing.worker.start_worker with the Redis service and a transactional DB, because results go to the django-db result backend.

Add the Redis service (public.ecr.aws/u7h0g2s9/rhinofcp/redis:7.4.3, as in the `test` job) to the API Tests job for the contract run. RQ jobs such as task_response_job are not in scope here; FakeOnPremClient.complete_task reaches that code directly.

import uuid
from collections import namedtuple

from celery.canvas import maybe_signature
from kombu.serialization import dumps, loads

from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.celery_tasks.app import app

SentTask = namedtuple("SentTask", "name args kwargs options task_id")


class FakeTaskQueue:
    """Stands in for the broker: send_task() records, drain() runs, oldest first. Unlike CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER,
    arguments go through our serializer (pickle) as on Redis, and nothing runs until the test asks."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.sent: list[SentTask] = []
        self.ran: list[SentTask] = []

    def send_task(self, name, args=None, kwargs=None, task_id=None, **options):  # replaces app.send_task
        content_type, encoding, body = dumps((args or (), kwargs or {}), serializer=app.conf.task_serializer)
        args, kwargs = loads(body, content_type, encoding, accept=app.conf.accept_content)
        self.sent.append(SentTask(name, tuple(args), kwargs, options, task_id or str(uuid.uuid4())))
        return app.AsyncResult(self.sent[-1].task_id)  # callers read .id; tests call drain(), never .get()

    def drain(self) -> list[SentTask]:
        while self.sent:
            task = self.sent.pop(0)
            result = app.tasks[task.name].apply(task.args, task.kwargs, task_id=task.task_id, headers=task.options.get("headers"))
            result.get(propagate=True)  # the task's own exception, raised in the test
            if chain := list(task.options.get("chain") or []):
                next_sig = maybe_signature(chain.pop(), app=app)  # Celery keeps the rest of a chain reversed
                next_sig.apply_async(() if next_sig.immutable else (result.result,), chain=chain or None)
            self.ran.append(task)
        return self.ran

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from faker import Faker

from fcp_common.rhinoTaskServices.task_common import TaskStatus, TaskType
from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.models.dataset import Dataset

from integration_test_utils.rhino_api_wrapper import RhinoAPITestWrapper

SCHEMA_CSVS = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "rhinoCore" / "integration-tests" / "pytest_fixtures"
fake = Faker()


@dataclass
class Site:
    api: RhinoAPITestWrapper  # logged in as the site's user, on the in-process transport (see builder.site())
    workgroup_uid: str
    email: str
    password: str  # generated per test; fake


def data_schema(site: Site, project_uid: str, csv_name: str = "Pneumonia Input Schema.csv") -> str:
    return site.api.create_schema(project_uid, SCHEMA_CSVS / csv_name)


def dataset(site: Site, project_uid: str, schema_uid: str, onprem_client, import_output: dict) -> str:
    """Import through POST datasets/ like the UI does; the fake client "runs" the import task.
    sync=False on purpose: a sync import polls the DB in this thread while waiting, so the fake could never answer."""
    created = site.api.create_dataset(fake.catch_phrase(), project_uid, schema_uid, "/rhino_data/fake.csv", sync=False)
    task = next(t for t in reversed(onprem_client.scheduled) if t.task_type == TaskType.DATASET_IMPORT)
    onprem_client.complete_task(task.task_uid, TaskStatus.COMPLETED, import_output)  # fake rows, made with Faker
    status = site.api.api.make_call("GET", f"datasets/{created['uid']}/")["data"]["import_status"]
    assert status == Dataset.ImportStatusTypes.COMPLETE, status
    return created["uid"]

#!/bin/bash
# Gate D on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 VM, plus the numbers G7-16 needs to size lab-runner-set.
# Usage: ci/gate-d.sh /absolute/path/to/fcp   (no cloud credentials, kubeconfig or VPN on this machine)
set -euo pipefail
fcp="${1:?usage: ci/gate-d.sh /absolute/path/to/fcp}"
lab_root="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)"
out="gate-d-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
mkdir -p "$out"

{ uname -a; nproc; free -g; df -h /var/lib/docker; docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'; docker compose version; } > "$out/host.txt"

# Sample per-container CPU and memory every 10 s while the Lab runs.
( while sleep 10; do
    docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}},{{.CPUPerc}},{{.MemUsage}}' | sed "s/^/$(date +%s),/" >> "$out/stats.csv"
  done ) &
sampler=$!
trap 'kill "$sampler"' EXIT

for run in cold warm; do  # the warm run reuses the images the cold run built
  start=$(date +%s)
  "$lab_root/ci/rehearse.sh" "$fcp" > "$out/$run.json" || echo "$run FAILED" >> "$out/timings.txt"
  echo "$run $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s" >> "$out/timings.txt"
done

docker system df -v > "$out/disk.txt"  # the lab README expects about 11 GB of images per source hash
du -sh "${FCP_LAB_HOME:-$HOME/.fcp-lab}" >> "$out/disk.txt"
echo "Attach $out/ to the ticket. Keep the lab's reports/ on this VM; they hold the Lab's own evidence."

    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    needs: check-changes
    if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' && needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    env:
      ENV: QA
      DJANGO_SECRET_KEY: rhino
      DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: rhinoCloud.rhinoDjango.settings
      # ...plus whatever settings.py reads at import time (copy from the `test` job); no database is used
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        run: uv sync --frozen --no-install-project && echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Export the v2 schema for the merge base and for this commit
        run: |
          git worktree add "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)"
          # This commit's export script runs against both trees, so the first run already has a base.
          PYTHONPATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/base/cloud:$RUNNER_TEMP/base/common" python cloud/rhinoCloud/scripts/export_openapi.py > "$RUNNER_TEMP/base.yaml"
          PYTHONPATH="$PWD/cloud:$PWD/common" python cloud/rhinoCloud/scripts/export_openapi.py > "$RUNNER_TEMP/head.yaml"
      - name: Fail on breaking changes
        # $RUNNER_TEMP sits on the work volume the dind sidecar shares; pin the image by digest
        run: >
          docker run --rm -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:/work" -v "$PWD/cloud/rhinoCloud:/cfg:ro" tufin/oasdiff@sha256:<digest>
          breaking /work/base.yaml /work/head.yaml --fail-on ERR --format githubactions
          --err-ignore /cfg/openapi-breaking-ignore.txt

title: [BE] Agent-friendly test output: failures.md, JUnit and a fixed seed
what: Make `poe api-test` write reports/failures.md (a short, complete report per failing test) and reports/junit.xml, and run with a fixed random seed that the report prints.
why: An agent fixes its own mistakes only when the failure is easy to read. A 3,000-line log fills its context; a one-page report with the file, the error and an exact rerun command does not.
how: Add tests_api/plugins/agent_report.py (sketch) and register it with `pytest_plugins` in tests_api/conftest.py. Under xdist only the controller writes the report.
Per failure: test id, file:line, the first line of the error, the last 40 lines of the traceback and a rerun command with the seed. Cap it at 20 failures and point to junit.xml for the rest.

Add the Poe task to the root pyproject.toml next to backend-integration-tests: `api-test = { cmd = "uv run --frozen --group api-tests pytest tests_api -n auto --randomly-seed=1009 --junitxml=reports/junit.xml -q --tb=short", cwd = "cloud/rhinoCloud", help = "..." }`; add reports/ to .gitignore.

pytest-randomly with a fixed seed shuffles tests in the same order every run and reseeds random, Faker and factory_boy, so a failure reproduces. Decide with the guild whether the nightly uses a new seed each night to find order bugs.
Try it: break one test on purpose, give Claude Code only reports/failures.md, and check it can fix the test without opening the log.

code.text:
import os
from pathlib import Path

MAX_FAILURES = 20
TAIL_LINES = 40


def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):
    if hasattr(session.config, "workerinput"):  # an xdist worker: the controller writes the report
        return
    stats = session.config.pluginmanager.get_plugin("terminalreporter").stats
    failed = [r for r in stats.get("failed", []) + stats.get("error", []) if r.when in ("setup", "call")]
    seed = session.config.getoption("randomly_seed", default=None)
    lines = [f"# API tests: {len(failed)} failing (seed {seed})", ""]
    for report in failed[:MAX_FAILURES]:
        crash = getattr(report.longrepr, "reprcrash", None)
        lines += [
            f"## {report.nodeid}",
            f"- where: {crash.path}:{crash.lineno}" if crash else "- where: fixture or setup error",
            f"- error: {crash.message.splitlines()[0]}" if crash else "",
            "```",
            *report.longreprtext.splitlines()[-TAIL_LINES:],
            "```",
            f"- rerun: `cd cloud/rhinoCloud && uv run --group api-tests pytest tests_api/{report.nodeid} --randomly-seed={seed}`",
            "",
        ]
    if len(failed) > MAX_FAILURES:
        lines.append(f"{len(failed) - MAX_FAILURES} more failures are in reports/junit.xml")
    out = Path(os.environ.get("API_TEST_REPORT_DIR", "reports"))
    out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (out / "failures.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) if failed else "# API tests: all passed\n")

title: [BE] Lint new migrations with django-migration-linter and Squawk
needs: G4 checking guide gets a line for this check
what: In cloud CI, check every migration added since main twice: django-migration-linter for changes that break the code still running during a deploy, and Squawk on the SQL from `manage.py sqlmigrate` for locks and table rewrites that hurt a live Postgres.
why: Agents will write migrations. A column drop or a table rewrite looks harmless in a diff but breaks old pods during a rollout or locks a big table, and both tools catch this before review.
how: Add django-migration-linter to the `test` dependency group, and to INSTALLED_APPS only when RHINO_IS_RUNNING_UNIT_TESTS=1 (in rhinoDjango/settings_test.py).

Add .squawk.toml at the repo root: pg_version 17.6 (what CI and the Lab run; check the prod RDS version), assume_in_transaction = true (Django wraps migrations in a transaction), and excluded rules with a reason each.
Start advisory for 2 weeks (continue-on-error), go through the findings with the BE guild, then make it blocking. Exceptions are per migration, with a comment, and added by a person.
Client migrations (rhinoAgent, rhinoRawDataHandler) run on customer machines at upgrade time; add them later if the guild wants it.

code.text:
# After "Check for missing migrations". This job's checkout needs `fetch-depth: 0` for the merge base.
      - name: Lint new migrations (django-migration-linter + Squawk)
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        continue-on-error: true  # advisory for the first 2 weeks, then remove this line
        run: |
          base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
          ./manage.py lintmigrations --git-commit-id "$base"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/sql"
          new=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$base" -- rhinoCore/migrations/ | grep -E '/[0-9]{4}_[^/]+\.py$' || true)
          for file in $new; do
            name=$(basename "$file" .py)
            ./manage.py sqlmigrate rhinoCore "$name" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/sql/$name.sql"
          done
          if [ -n "$new" ]; then
            # .squawk.toml at the repo root: pg_version, assume_in_transaction = true, excluded rules with reasons
            uvx --from squawk-cli squawk --config ../../.squawk.toml "$RUNNER_TEMP"/sql/*.sql
          fi

from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.services.permission_service import remove_rhino_admin_from_permissions

def test_project_collab_permission_endpoint(api_client, builder):

        PermissionPersona.RHINO_ADMIN.name,

    api_client.add_collaborator(project_uid, collaborator.workgroup_uid, permissions=custom)

title: [BE] Add a buf breaking check for the cloud-client gRPC protos
needs: G4 checking guide gets a line for this check
what: Add common/buf.yaml and a `buf breaking` step in cloud CI that compares common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/*.proto with the merge base on main.
why: On-prem clients upgrade later than the cloud, so a removed field or RPC breaks customers who have not upgraded yet. The cloud dispatches agent calls by method name (AgentRpcRequest.method_name), so even a rename that looks safe on the wire breaks them.
how: Add common/buf.yaml (sketch). The module root is common/ because `make protoc` uses --proto_path=common, so buf sees the same file paths as the generated _pb2 modules.
Use the PACKAGE rule set, not WIRE: WIRE allows deleting or renaming RPCs, which our method-name dispatch cannot survive.

In the cloud-ci.yml lint job (it already runs the protoc drift check), set fetch-depth: 0, add bufbuild/buf-action with setup_only: true, then run `buf breaking common --against ".git#ref=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main),subdir=common"`.
The protos have no `reserved` entries today. Add a short note to common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/README.md: reserve a removed field's number and name instead of reusing them.
A deliberate break needs a person and a plan for old clients; add one line about this to Nova's checking guide (G4).

code.text:
# Module root is common/ because `make protoc` runs with --proto_path=common, so buf sees
# fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/*.proto with the same paths as the generated _pb2 files.
version: v2
modules:
  - path: .
breaking:
  use:
    # PACKAGE, not WIRE: AgentRpcRequest carries the RPC by method_name, so deleting or renaming an RPC
    # breaks older on-prem clients even though the bytes still parse. Clients upgrade later than the cloud.
    - PACKAGE
  except:
    # We never use the proto JSON mapping between cloud and client (gRPC binary only). Confirm with the BE guild.
    - FIELD_SAME_JSON_NAME

With Nave, add a lab command that builds a source tree's images and pushes them to a registry, and a way for `lab up` to pull them instead of building. The lab only builds locally today, so the flags in the sketch are placeholders.
Add .github/workflows/_lab-images-reusable.yml (sketch) on lab-runner-set: OIDC to the GitHubActions role in 123456789012, amazon-ecr-login, skip if the tag exists, else build and push.

name: FCP Lab images (reusable)
on:
  workflow_call:
    outputs:
      tag: { value: "${{ jobs.images.outputs.tag }}" }

jobs:
  images:
    runs-on: lab-runner-set
    permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
    concurrency: lab-images-${{ github.sha }}  # cloud-ci, client-ci and frontend-ci on one commit share one build
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.build.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        id: lab-token
        with:  # decide which App; read-only, on the lab repo only
          app-id: ${{ secrets.LAB_READER_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.LAB_READER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          repositories: fcp-local-lab  # final repo name to confirm with Nave (moved into the org in G7-09)
          permission-contents: read
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with: { repository: RhinoHealth/fcp-local-lab, path: .lab, token: "${{ steps.lab-token.outputs.token }}" }
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with: { aws-region: us-east-1, role-to-assume: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActions" }
      - uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2
      - name: Build and push once per commit
        id: build
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_SHA}-lab$(python3 .lab/lab --version)"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          aws ecr describe-images --repository-name fcp-lab-cloud --image-ids imageTag="$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0
          # Placeholder CLI: the lab only builds locally today; agree the command with Nave.
          python3 .lab/lab build --source "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --push "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/fcp-lab-{component}:$tag"

"""The latest *published* rhino-health SDK against this commit's API, over real HTTP (pytest-django live_server).
The API Tests job runs: uv run --group api-tests --with rhino-health==$SDK_VERSION pytest tests_api/sdk_smoke"""

import pytest

rh = pytest.importorskip("rhino_health")  # in no uv group on purpose: CI installs the released wheel

pytestmark = [pytest.mark.sdk_smoke, pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)]  # live_server needs committed rows


@pytest.fixture
def sdk(live_server, builder):
    site = builder.site()  # a fake workgroup and user, created through the API
    session = rh.login(username=site.email, password=site.password, rhino_api_url=f"{live_server.url}/api/")
    return session, site


def test_published_sdk_creates_and_finds_a_project(sdk):
    from rhino_health.lib.endpoints.project.project_dataclass import ProjectCreateInput

    session, site = sdk
    project = session.project.add_project(
        ProjectCreateInput(name="SDK smoke", description="", type="Validation", primary_workgroup_uid=site.workgroup_uid)
    )
    assert session.project.get_project_by_name("sdk smoke").uid == project.uid  # the name search ignores case

Checks, one line each with its fix: node and npm from frontend/package.json engines (>=24.15.0, >=11.14.1), Python 3.13 through uv, `uv sync --check` for cloud/rhinoCloud (and client), Docker memory of at least 16 GiB (FCP Lab needs it), the rhino-net network, and poe itself.

Git hooks: after `npm install`, husky sets core.hooksPath to frontend/.husky/_, so the black, isort and flake8 hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml never run on commit. The doctor reports this and points to `poe verify`; decide with the BE guild whether husky's pre-commit should also call pre-commit for Python files.
--fix runs only safe local commands (uv python install, make sync-deps, docker network create) and prints them; it never touches credentials, ~/.aws or Docker volumes.
--json prints one JSON object per check for machines; the nightly sandbox image build uses it (G7-25).
Try it on two laptops, one of them a new joiner's if possible, and fix the three most confusing messages.

code.text:
"""poe doctor: check a local fcp setup; --fix runs the safe local fixes; --json is for the sandbox image build."""
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ENGINES = json.loads((ROOT / "frontend" / "package.json").read_text())["engines"]  # node >=24.15.0, npm >=11.14.1


def _run(*cmd: str) -> str | None:
    done = shutil.which(cmd[0]) and subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT)
    return done.stdout.strip() if done and done.returncode == 0 else None


def _at_least(have: str | None, want: str) -> bool:  # "v24.16.0" >= ">=24.15.0"
    return have is not None and [int(p) for p in have.strip("v").split(".")] >= [int(p) for p in want.strip(">=").split(".")]


CHECKS = [  # (what, passes, fix, safe for --fix); npm, poe and the rhino-net network follow the same pattern
    ("node " + ENGINES["node"], lambda: _at_least(_run("node", "--version"), ENGINES["node"]), "nvm install", False),
    ("Python 3.13 (uv)", lambda: _run("uv", "python", "find", "3.13"), "uv python install 3.13", True),
    ("cloud venv = uv.lock", lambda: _run("uv", "sync", "--check", "--directory", "cloud/rhinoCloud"), "make -C cloud/rhinoCloud sync-deps", True),
    ("Docker >= 16 GiB (FCP Lab)", lambda: int(_run("docker", "info", "-f", "{{.MemTotal}}") or 0) >= 16 * 2**30, "raise Docker's memory limit", False),
    ("Python commit hooks (husky owns core.hooksPath, so black/isort/flake8 never run)", lambda: _run("git", "config", "core.hooksPath") is None, "run `poe verify` before you push", False),
]


def main(fix: bool = False, as_json: bool = False) -> None:
    results = [(what, bool(passes()), how, safe) for what, passes, how, safe in CHECKS]
    for what, ok, how, safe in results:
        if fix and safe and not ok:
            subprocess.run(how, shell=True, cwd=ROOT)  # local commands only: never credentials, ~/.aws or volumes
        print(json.dumps({"check": what, "ok": ok, "fix": how}) if as_json else f"{'ok ' if ok else 'FIX'}  {what}  {'' if ok else '-> ' + how}")
    raise SystemExit(0 if all(ok for _, ok, _, _ in results) else 1)

title: [DevOps] Validate gitops charts: helm lint and helm template | kubeconform
what: A gitops workflow that, for each chart a PR changes, runs helm lint and renders every <env>-values.yaml with helm template piped into kubeconform.
why: gitops has no checks today, so a typo in a values file reaches Argo CD as a sync error on a real cluster. Rendering and schema-checking every environment catches most of that in a minute, with no cluster access.
how: Create .github/workflows/chart-checks.yml on pull_request, runs-on gitops-runner-set, actions pinned by SHA.
Changed charts are the folders with a Chart.yaml that the PR touches (cloud/rhino-server, cloud/temporal, frontend/dashboard, argocd/argocd-apps, and so on).

Per chart: `helm dependency build` (Chart.lock is committed and *.tgz is gitignored; use Nexus's helm proxy if a public repo rate-limits), `helm lint`, then `helm template` for each *-values.yaml piped into `kubeconform -strict -summary`.

CRDs (ExternalSecret, KEDA ScaledObject, HTTPRoute, Argo CD Application) come from the datreeio CRDs-catalog schema location. Use the oldest Kubernetes version among the product clusters for -kubernetes-version.
First run: list the current failures per environment in the PR and fix the cheap ones; skip the rest with a comment and an owner.

code.text:
name: Chart checks
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions: { contents: read }

jobs:
  charts:
    runs-on: gitops-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@<sha> # pin by SHA
      - name: Install kubeconform
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" && echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          curl -sSL https://github.com/yannh/kubeconform/releases/download/v0.7.0/kubeconform-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin"
      - name: Lint and render every environment of each changed chart
        run: |
          status=0
          charts=$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u \
            | while read -r d; do while [ "$d" != . ] && [ ! -f "$d/Chart.yaml" ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; [ -f "$d/Chart.yaml" ] && echo "$d"; done | sort -u)
          for chart in $charts; do
            helm dependency build "$chart" >/dev/null && helm lint "$chart" || status=1
            for values in "$chart"/*-values.yaml; do
              [ -e "$values" ] || continue
              helm template ci "$chart" -f "$values" | kubeconform -strict -summary -kubernetes-version 1.36.0 \
                -schema-location default \
                -schema-location 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datreeio/CRDs-catalog/main/{{.Group}}/{{.ResourceKind}}_{{.ResourceAPIVersion}}.json' \
                || { echo "::error file=$values::does not render to valid manifests"; status=1; }
            done
          done
          exit $status

title: [DevOps] Run poe doctor in the nightly ai-agent-sandbox image build

- name: Prove a fresh fcp setup works (poe doctor)
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: uvx --from poethepoet poe doctor --json
    chdir: "{{ fcp_checkout_dir }}"  # the image's fcp checkout; take the variable name from G3's playbook
  become: true
  become_user: "{{ sandbox_user }}"  # the user Nova runs as, so file ownership matches
  register: doctor

name: FCP Lab smoke (reusable)
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      image_tag: { required: true, type: string }
      suite: { required: false, type: string, default: smoke }  # G7-33 passes frontend-e2e

jobs:
  smoke:
    name: FCP Lab smoke
    runs-on: lab-runner-set
    permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
    concurrency:
      group: lab-smoke-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}  # a newer push cancels the older run; not a shared lock
      cancel-in-progress: true
    env:
      LAB_ID: ci-${{ github.run_id }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }  # compare needs the merge base with origin/main
      # ...lab checkout, AWS OIDC and ECR login as in _lab-images-reusable.yml
      - name: Boot the Lab from this commit's images
        run: python3 .lab/lab up --source "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --id "$LAB_ID" --mode snapshot --images "${{ inputs.image_tag }}"  # --images: see G7-20
      - name: Smoke suite  # inputs.suite == 'frontend-e2e' runs the lab's whole allowlist instead (G7-33)
        run: |
          python3 .lab/lab test "$LAB_ID" --suite core --json > core.json
          python3 .lab/lab test "$LAB_ID" --suite frontend-e2e --spec not-found-page.spec.ts --json > e2e.json  # + the agreed specs
          python3 .lab/lab exec "$LAB_ID" web-service -- pytest tests_api -m contract --target lab  # path: check with Nave
      - name: Compare with main, only because something failed
        if: failure()
        run: python3 .lab/lab compare --source "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --id "cmp-$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --json > compare.json || true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with: { name: lab-smoke-reports, path: "*.json" }  # plus the lab's reports/ directory for traces

# Called from the existing pytest_collection_modifyitems (which already shuffles tests and adds trace ids).
# Register the marker in cloud/rhinoCloud/pytest.ini:
#   quarantine(ticket): known flaky; still runs and reports, but does not turn the nightly red


def _apply_quarantine(items: list[pytest.Item]) -> None:
    for item in items:
        marker = item.get_closest_marker("quarantine")
        if marker is None:
            continue
        ticket = marker.kwargs["ticket"]  # required: every quarantined test has a Jira ticket and an owner
        # Non-strict xfail: the test still runs; junit.xml shows it as skipped with this reason, so
        # scripts/nightly_history.py can list quarantined tests and their tickets.
        item.add_marker(pytest.mark.xfail(reason=f"quarantined, see {ticket}", strict=False))


# In a test module, added by a person after triage (agents never quarantine, skip or delete tests):
#
#   @pytest.mark.quarantine(ticket="RH-0000")  # placeholder key
#   def test_...(api_client): ...
#
# The 10 tests with @pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=N) today get a flaky-test ticket each; decide with the guild
# whether to replace their reruns with quarantine, so the flakiness shows in the history.

  # integration-tests-gcp: the same `if:`. `publish` already needs both and only runs on main.

title: [DevOps] Post read-only Terragrunt plans on infrastructure PRs
needs: G0 Vault narrowing (read-only Vault role for plans)
what: A pull_request workflow in the infrastructure repo that runs `terragrunt plan` with TerraformPlanRole for the units a PR changes and posts one comment with the result per unit. It never applies.
why: Reviewers and agents see the real effect of an infra change on the PR instead of a plan pasted by hand. Applying stays a person's job.
how: Create .github/workflows/terragrunt-plan.yml (sketch) on pull_request, runs-on infrastructure-runner-set, TG_ROLE_NAME=TerraformPlanRole, OIDC to GitHubActionsTerraformPlan.
Units = folders with a changed terragrunt.hcl. For a module-only change, find the units that use the module with Terragrunt 1.1's include-units-reading option (check its exact flag name).
`terragrunt plan -lock=false -input=false -no-color` per unit. Never write plan files with -out: a plan file holds secret values in plain text.
Post one sticky comment: per unit the "Plan: X to add, Y to change, Z to destroy" line and the changed resource addresses; the full output stays in the job log of this private repo.
No apply, destroy or workflow_dispatch anywhere in this workflow; agents can read the comment but not act on infrastructure.

code.text:
name: "[TERRAGRUNT] Plan on PRs (read-only)"
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['terraform/**', 'modules/**', 'multi_tenant/**', 'single_tenant/**']

permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read, pull-requests: write }

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: infrastructure-runner-set
    env:
      TG_ROLE_NAME: TerraformPlanRole  # read by account.hcl (G7-30); never TerraformDeploymentRole here
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@<sha> # pin by SHA
        with: { aws-region: us-east-1, role-to-assume: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActionsTerraformPlan" }
      - name: Install Tofu and Terragrunt
        env: { TENV_GITHUB_TOKEN: "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" }
        run: tenv tofu install && tenv tg install
      - name: Plan the changed units (read-only, no lock, no plan files)
        run: |
          git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep 'terragrunt.hcl$' | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u > units.txt
          # Module-only changes: add the units that read the module (Terragrunt 1.1 include-units-reading; check the flag).
          while read -r unit; do
            (cd "$unit" && terragrunt plan -lock=false -input=false -no-color) > "plan-${unit//\//_}.txt" 2>&1 || true
          done < units.txt
      - name: One comment with the summary per unit
        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }
        run: .github/scripts/post_plan_comment.sh units.txt  # "Plan: X to add, Y to change, Z to destroy" + addresses

title: [DevOps] Move the frontend PR gate from qa-front-end to FCP Lab
needs: G0 ruleset makes the new gate a required check
what: In frontend-ci.yaml, pull requests stop calling _frontend-int-tests-reusable-{aws,gcp}.yml (lock frontend_integration_tests_{aws,gcp} on qa-front-end) and run the pr/ Playwright project on the Lab instead; QA keeps main, the nightly and releases.
why: frontend-ci is the only CI that runs on pull_request, and every FE PR queues for qa-front-end today. The e2e_tests alls-green job inside the reusable workflows is the gate that has to move with it.
how: Add an e2e-lab job that calls _lab-smoke-reusable.yml with suite frontend-e2e (the lab's allowlist of 24 pr/ and nightly/ spec files). List the specs the Lab can't run (the lab's AGENTS.md names them, such as GCP VMs or a real AWS bucket) and keep only those on the QA nightly.
Move the e2e_tests re-actors/alls-green gate out of _frontend-int-tests-reusable-aws.yml and -gcp.yml into frontend-ci.yaml (sketch), so one gate covers the Lab on PRs and QA on main.
integration-tests-aws and -gcp get `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`; check whether build-e2e-app is still needed on PRs once QA no longer runs there.
merge-frontend-coverage reads e2e coverage from the QA runs: point it at the Lab job's artifact, or accept no e2e coverage on PRs (decide with the FE guild).
Test this on a draft PR. Don't dispatch frontend-ci on a branch: that deploys over main's dev dashboard and Storybook.
Ask G0 to make e2e_tests required in the main ruleset, as in G7-31.

code.text:
e2e-lab:
    name: E2E on FCP Lab
    needs: [check-changes, lab-images]
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_lab-smoke-reusable.yml
    with:
      image_tag: ${{ needs.lab-images.outputs.tag }}
      suite: frontend-e2e  # the lab's allowlist instead of the short smoke list
    secrets: inherit

  integration-tests-aws:
    name: "I&T - AWS"
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_frontend-int-tests-reusable-aws.yml
    needs: [check-changes, build-e2e-app]
    # qa-front-end (lock frontend_integration_tests_aws) after merge, nightly and releases only
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true')
    # with: ...unchanged

  e2e_tests:  # moved here from the reusable workflows: one gate for the Lab on PRs and for QA on main
    if: always()
    needs: [e2e-lab, integration-tests-aws, integration-tests-gcp]
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          allowed-skips: e2e-lab, integration-tests-aws, integration-tests-gcp
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

title: [DevOps] argocd-diff-preview for gitops PRs on a throw-away kind cluster
what: A gitops pull_request workflow that renders the Argo CD applications for main and for the PR on a throw-away kind cluster with argocd-diff-preview and posts the rendered manifest diff as a PR comment.
why: A values change can touch many environments at once, and reviewers can't see that from the diff alone. Seeing the rendered result before merge catches surprises, and nothing ever syncs to a real cluster.
how: argocd/argocd-apps is a Helm chart that renders Applications from <env>-values.yaml and is installed with helm on inf, so there are no plain Application files for the tool to find. Render them for both branches first (sketch).

Run dagandersen/argocd-diff-preview (pinned) in docker; the kind cluster runs inside the dind sidecar of gitops-runner-set and is gone with the pod. Every destination in our apps is a remote product cluster; the tool renders locally and never contacts them.
Give it a read-only token for the gitops repo (and any private chart source); no cluster credentials at all.
Post the diff as one comment, edited on each push; for very large diffs post the summary and attach the full diff as an artifact.
No argocd sync, apply or workflow_dispatch anywhere in this workflow.

code.text:
name: Argo CD diff preview
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write }

jobs:
  diff:
    runs-on: gitops-runner-set  # ARC dind: kind runs inside the dind sidecar; nothing reaches a real cluster
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # pin by SHA
        with: { path: pull-request }
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha>
        with: { ref: main, path: main }
      - name: Render the Applications (argocd-apps is a Helm chart installed with helm on inf, not plain YAML)
        run: |
          for side in main pull-request; do
            for values in "$side"/argocd/argocd-apps/*-values.yaml; do
              helm template apps "$side/argocd/argocd-apps" -f "$values" > "$side/rendered-apps-$(basename "$values")"
            done
          done
      - name: Diff on a throw-away kind cluster
        run: |
          docker run --network host -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
            -v "$PWD/main:/base-branch" -v "$PWD/pull-request:/target-branch" -v "$PWD/output:/output" \
            -e TARGET_BRANCH="${{ github.head_ref }}" -e REPO="${{ github.repository }}" \
            dagandersen/argocd-diff-preview:<pinned version>
      - name: Post the diff
        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }
        run: |
          gh pr comment "${{ github.event.number }}" --edit-last --body-file output/diff.md \
            || gh pr comment "${{ github.event.number }}" --body-file output/diff.md

title: [BE] Nightly mutation report on files that agent PRs changed
needs: G0 rhino-ai-agents GitHub App (to find agent PRs); G5 coverage-gap routine reads the report
what: A nightly, advisory job that runs mutmut on the cloud files that agent PRs changed the day before, judged by the API layer, and publishes the surviving mutants.
why: A test suite that passes no matter what the code does gives agents false confidence. Surviving mutants show where the tests are weak, and they are the input for the coverage-gap routine, in the pattern Meta's ACH used.
how: Add .github/workflows/cloud-mutation-nightly.yml (sketch): schedule only, never a required check, on fcp-runner-set with the same Postgres service and env as the API Tests job.

Files: merged PRs from the last day authored by the rhino-ai-agents App (`gh pr list --search "author:app/rhino-ai-agents merged:>=<date>"`), keeping cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/**/*.py without tests and migrations, at most 10 files a night.

mutmut 3 with a generated setup.cfg [mutmut] section: paths_to_mutate = those files, tests_dir = tests_api/. Only the API layer judges mutants, because rhinoCore/tests run on manage.py test, not pytest.

Check that mutmut 3's mutants/ copy is what `rhinoCloud.rhinoCore...` imports (the code is imported through PYTHONPATH=cloud). If it is not, run from cloud/ with rhinoCloud/... paths, or try cosmic-ray, and say which in the PR.

Report: killed, survived and timed-out counts per file, plus the surviving mutants' diffs, as the job summary and an artifact. The weekly run review reads it; the G5 coverage-gap routine turns survivors into test proposals.

code.text:
name: "[CLOUD] - Mutation report (advisory)"
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4 * * *' # after the 02:44 UTC cloud nightly

jobs:
  mutation:
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    # services and env: the same Postgres service and env as the API Tests job in cloud-ci.yml
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Cloud files that agent PRs changed yesterday
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh pr list --state merged --limit 50 --search "author:app/rhino-ai-agents merged:>=$(date -u -d yesterday +%F)" \
            --json files --jq '.[].files[].path' \
            | grep -E '^cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/.+\.py$' | grep -vE '/(tests|migrations|integration-tests)/' \
            | sed 's|^cloud/rhinoCloud/||' | sort -u | head -n 10 > touched.txt || true
      - name: Mutate only those files; only the API layer judges the mutants
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        run: |
          [ -s ../../touched.txt ] || { echo "No agent-changed cloud files yesterday"; exit 0; }
          printf '[mutmut]\npaths_to_mutate=%s\ntests_dir=tests_api/\n' "$(paste -sd, ../../touched.txt)" > setup.cfg
          uv run --frozen --group api-tests --with mutmut mutmut run || true
          uv run --frozen --group api-tests --with mutmut mutmut results > ../../mutation-report.txt
      - name: Report (advisory, never a required check)
        if: hashFiles('mutation-report.txt') != ''
        run: |
          { echo "## Surviving mutants in agent-changed files"; echo '```'; cat mutation-report.txt; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: hashFiles('mutation-report.txt') != ''
        with: { name: mutation-report, path: mutation-report.txt }
